5.01.b:
### Parts of a typical vertebra
- **Body** in front → **pedicles** → **laminae** meet behind → **spinous process**; ring = **spinal canal**
  [[FIG: Fig 5.1 · 5.01
- **Transverse process** → between pedicle and lamina · 4 **articular processes** → 2 superior + 2 inferior = **facet joints**
- **Pars interarticularis** → strut between the articular processes, best seen on a **coronal** cut · **foramen** → between two pedicles, root exits
- Count → **33** = 7 cervical · 12 thoracic · 5 lumbar · 5 sacral (fused) · 4 coccygeal

### Which region? — one look
[[FIG: Fig 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 · 5.01
| Feature | Cervical | Thoracic | Lumbar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Body | Small, oval, **uncinate process** (uncus) | **Heart-shaped**, costal facets | Big, **kidney-shaped** |
| Transverse process | **Foramen transversarium** | **Costal facet** for the rib tubercle | Long, thin, no facet |
| Spinous process | Short, **bifid** (C3–C6) | Long, points **down** | Short, square, **hatchet** |
| Facet plane | ≈45° → all movements | **Coronal** → rotation | **Sagittal** → flexion–extension |

- Hold it → hole in the transverse process = **cervical** · rib facet on the body = **thoracic** · neither = **lumbar**

| Vertebra | Why atypical | Point to |
|---|---|---|
| **C1, C2** | No body / dens | → 5.02 |
| **C7** | Vertebra prominens | Long **non-bifid** spine · small foramen transversarium (veins only; artery runs **in front**) |
| **T1** | Cervical-looking body | **Full facet** for rib 1 + demifacet for rib 2 |
| **T10** | One rib only | **Single** facet for rib 10 |
| **T11–T12** | No rib tubercle facet | Single facet · **no transverse-process facet** · T12 lower facets lumbar-type |
| **L5** | Biggest, wedge | Body taller in front · **thick transverse process** from body + pedicle → iliolumbar ligament |

5.02.b:
### Hold C1 & C2 → point & say
[[FIG: Fig 5.12, 5.13, 5.14 · 5.02
| Point to | C1 (atlas) | C2 (axis) |
|---|---|---|
| Front | **Anterior arch** + facet for the dens | **Dens** (odontoid) |
| Side | **Lateral masses** → up to the condyles, down to C2 | Superior facets → C1; **pars** → hangman's fracture |
| Back | Posterior arch + **groove for the vertebral artery** (upper surface) | Big **bifid spine** → landmark on X-ray |
| What it lacks | **No body**, no spinous process | — |

- **Dens = the embryonic body of C1**, fused to C2
- O–C1 → nodding ("yes") · C1–C2 → rotation ("no"), a **pivot synovial** joint

### Ligaments of the craniocervical junction
[[FIG: Fig 5.15, 5.16 · 5.02
| Ligament | Runs | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Transverse** | Lateral mass → lateral mass, behind the dens | Holds the dens → **main C1–C2 stabiliser** |
| **Cruciate** | Transverse + vertical bands | Same, with up/down bands |
| **Alar** | Sides of the dens → occipital condyles | Limit rotation · avulsion = **type 3 condyle fracture** |
| **Apical** | Dens tip → foramen magnum | Weak, minor |
| **Tectorial membrane** | Covers them → continues down as the **PLL (posterior longitudinal ligament)** | Limits flexion |

- Mnemonic → "**T**ransverse **T**akes the load, **A**lar **A**nchors rotation, **T**ectorial **T**urns into the PLL"

### Numbers on the C1–C2 X-ray
- **ADI** (atlantodental interval) → normal **≤3 mm** · >5 mm → transverse torn · >7.5 mm → alar + apical too
  [[FIG: Fig 5.17, 5.18 · 5.02
- **PADI** (posterior ADI = space for the cord) → normal 18–19 mm · **<14 mm → surgery**; better predictor of neurology than ADI
- **Rule of Spence** → lateral masses overhang C2 by **>7 mm** (both sides added) → transverse ligament torn

PITFALL — ADI in children
- Handbook → adult values (≤3 mm); children have more cartilage and lax ligaments
- Say → "**3 mm in adults, up to 5 mm in children**" (Kim)

5.03.b:
### Uncovertebral joint (Luschka)
- **Uncus** of the body below → meets the body above · **cervical only** (C3–C7) · a "**pseudo-joint**" that blocks lateral slide
  [[FIG: Fig 5.19 · 5.03
- Osteophytes here → narrow the **foramen** from in front → radiculopathy
- **Vertebral artery lies just lateral** → the uncus is the **lateral limit** of anterior decompression

### Vertebral artery — the four parts
[[FIG: Fig 5.20, 5.21 · 5.03
| Part | Course | Point to |
|---|---|---|
| **V1** pre-foraminal | Subclavian → up in front of C7 transverse process | Enters the **C6** foramen |
| **V2** foraminal | Through the foramina **C6 → C1** | Lateral to the uncus |
| **V3** extradural | Out of C1 foramen → **behind the lateral mass** → groove on the C1 posterior arch | Suboccipital triangle |
| **V4** intradural | Pierces the dura → joins the other one | **Basilar** artery at the pons |

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "course of the vertebral artery in the cervical spine"
- **First branch of the subclavian** → passes in front of C7 → enters the **C6 foramen transversarium** (≈93%)
- **V2** → climbs through the foramina C6 → C1, **lateral to the uncinate processes**
- **V3** → leaves C1, curves **behind the C1 lateral mass**, lies in the **groove on top of the posterior arch** → suboccipital triangle
- **V4** → pierces the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane + dura → foramen magnum → joins the other → **basilar**
- At risk → anterior decompression too lateral · C1 posterior dissection too lateral · C1–C2 screws

- **Pedicle** → small, close to the artery (lateral) and root (below) → used mostly at **C2 and C7**

5.05.t: Joints, Disc & Ligaments of the Spine
5.05.b:
### Intervertebral disc
[[FIG: Fig 5.33, 5.34 · 5.05
| Part | Made of | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Annulus fibrosus** | **Type I** collagen | Resists **tension**, holds the nucleus |
| **Nucleus pulposus** | **Type II** collagen + proteoglycans, water | Resists **compression** |

- Discs → **¼ of spinal height**; first disc = **C2–C3**, last = L5–S1
- **Curves** come from **disc** shape (front taller than back), not vertebral body height
- Adult disc → **no vessels** → fed by diffusion through the endplates → poor healing

### Facet joints
- **Synovial** joints → from **C0–C1 to L5–S1** · **plane decides motion** (table in 5.01)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.35, 5.36 · 5.05
- Arthritic facet + thick ligamentum flavum → **lateral recess** stenosis

### Ligaments & Denis's three columns
[[FIG: Fig 5.37, 5.38 · 5.05
| Ligament | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **ALL** (anterior longitudinal) | Front of bodies, wide | Strong · torn in extension |
| **PLL** | Back of bodies, **inside the canal** | Narrow at the sides → **posterolateral** disc herniation |
| **Ligamentum flavum** | Lamina → lamina | Yellow (elastin) · thickens in stenosis |
| **Interspinous / supraspinous** | Between / over the spines | Part of the **PLC** (posterior ligamentous complex) |

| Column | Contains | Fracture that breaks it |
|---|---|---|
| **Anterior** | ALL + front ⅔ of body and disc | Compression → anterior only |
| **Middle** | Back ⅓ of body and disc + **PLL** | **Burst** → anterior + middle |
| **Posterior** | Arch + **PLC** | Flexion–distraction (**Chance**) → posterior first; fracture–dislocation → all 3 |

- Rule → **middle column broken = unstable** (Denis) → the bone in the middle column can enter the canal

5.06.t: Spinal Canal, Cord, Nerve Roots & Cauda Equina
5.06.b:
### Canal zones
[[FIG: Fig 5.39, 5.40 · 5.06
| Zone | Where | Walls |
|---|---|---|
| **Central canal** | Dural sac → cord + intradural roots | Front → body, disc, PLL · back → lamina, ligamentum flavum |
| **Zone 1 — lateral recess** | Dura → foramen | Back → **superior articular process** · front → disc **without PLL** |
| **Zone 2 — foramen** | The foramen itself | Pedicle above and below |
| **Zone 3 — extraforaminal** | Outside the foramen | No bony walls |

### Cord, conus & roots
- Cord ends at **L1–L2** in adults · at **L3 at birth**
  [[FIG: Fig 5.41 · 5.06
- Dural sac → **S2** · filum terminale → coccyx
- **31 segments** → 8 C, 12 T, 5 L, 5 S, 1 Co → 8 cervical nerves for 7 vertebrae

### Root–level rules
- **Cervical** → root exits **above** its pedicle (C6 root at C5–C6) · **C8** exits below C7
- From **T1 down** → root exits **below** its pedicle
  [[FIG: Fig 5.42, 5.43, 5.44 · 5.06
- Root leaves the dura **one level above** its foramen → long lumbar roots = **cauda equina**

| Disc | Paracentral (commonest) | Foraminal |
|---|---|---|
| **C6–C7** | **C7** root | **C7** root |
| **L4–L5** | **L5** root (traversing) | **L4** root (exiting) |

- Mnemonic → **F**oraminal = **E**arly number · para**C**entral = **L**ate number

### Cord tracts → incomplete cord syndromes (anatomy only)

| Tract | Carries | Crosses |
|---|---|---|
| **Lateral spinothalamic** | Pain, temperature | At **entry level** in the cord |
| **Posterior columns** | Proprioception, vibration, fine touch | In the **medulla** |
| **Lateral corticospinal** | Voluntary motor (80%) | In the **medulla** |

- Lamination → **arms medial, legs lateral** → central cord syndrome hits the **hands** most

| Syndrome | Mechanism | Lost | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Central cord** | Hyperextension, old spondylotic neck | Arms > legs, hands worst | Sacral sparing |
| **Anterior cord** | Hyperflexion | Motor + pain/temperature | **Posterior columns** · worst prognosis |
| **Brown-Séquard** | Hemisection | Same-side motor + position · opposite-side pain/temperature | Best prognosis |
| **Posterior cord** | Hyperextension (rare) | Deep sensation | Motor, pain |

5.07.t: Blood Supply of the Spinal Cord & Vertebrae
5.07.b:
### Arteries of the cord
- **One anterior spinal artery** → anterior ⅔ · **two posterior spinal** → posterior ⅓ · fed by **segmental arteries**
  [[FIG: Fig 5.47, 5.48 · 5.07
- **Artery of Adamkiewicz** → biggest feeder of the lower cord → **left** 77%, **T8–L1** 89%
- Danger → tying left segmental arteries at **T8–L1** (anterior thoracolumbar approach) → anterior cord syndrome · **watershed** = mid-thoracic cord

PITFALL — level of Adamkiewicz
- Netter → left T10–T12 · Orthobullets → left 75%, T8–L1 · Kim → left T8–L2
- Say → "**left side, T8–L1, most often T9–T12**" (Taterra 2019 meta-analysis)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "blood supply of the spinal cord"
- **Anterior spinal artery** (one) → front ⅔ → loss = anterior cord syndrome
- **Posterior spinal arteries** (two) → back ⅓ → posterior columns
- Reinforced by **segmental radicular arteries** at every level
- **Adamkiewicz** → largest one, usually **left T8–L1** → protect in left-sided thoracolumbar approaches
- **Watershed** in the mid-thoracic cord

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "embryology of the spine and why it matters"
- Somites beside the **notochord** → **sclerotome** + dermomyotome
- **Resegmentation** → half + half = one vertebra · disc at the line · 8 cervical somites → 7 vertebrae
- **Notochord → nucleus pulposus** · sclerotome → body, arch, annulus · tube → cord · crest → ganglia
- Errors → failure of **formation** (wedge, hemivertebra) vs **segmentation** (bar, block, Klippel-Feil) · tube → spina bifida · **dens = C1 body**
- Matters → **heart, kidney, cord** anomalies travel with them → MRI, echo, renal ultrasound

5.12.b:
HIGH YIELD — what is at risk, by region
- Anterior cervical → **RLN** (tracheo-oesophageal groove), oesophagus, carotid sheath · too lateral → **vertebral artery** (uncus = limit)
- Anterior cervical at C6 → **sympathetic chain** on longus colli → **Horner** · C1 posterior arch groove → **V3**
- Pedicle screw → dura (medial), **exiting root** (hugs the lower pedicle) · lumbar discectomy → **aorta / iliac vessels** in front of the annulus
- **ALIF** (anterior lumbar interbody fusion) → **superior hypogastric plexus** (L5–S1 promontory) → **retrograde ejaculation** up to 20% · left common iliac vein
- Anterior thoracolumbar → **Adamkiewicz**, left T8–L1

- Anterior crest graft → **LFCN** (lateral femoral cutaneous nerve) ≈15 mm below-medial to the ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine)
- Posterior crest graft → **superior cluneals** cross the crest 5–7 cm lateral to the PSIS (posterior superior iliac spine) · **superior gluteal artery** at the notch
- Approach-by-approach dangers → 5B

### Cervical X-ray — lines & numbers

- **Harris rule of 12** → dens–basion and basion–axial line <12 mm (Handbook)

| Line | Drawn from → to | Abnormal when dens tip |
|---|---|---|
| **Chamberlain** | Hard palate → opisthion | >3 mm above |
| **McGregor** | Hard palate → lowest occiput | >4.5 mm above |
| **McRae** | Basion → opisthion | Reaches the line (normal ≥5 mm below) |

(Handbook)
